title: add vpc control plane provisioning: multi-az subnets, interface endpoints, sgs, peering, route53
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Private installs of the control plane require multi-AZ networking and hardened connectivity. This PR extends the private-installer/terraform control-plane module to provision: multi-AZ private subnets, interface endpoints (EC2, SSM, ECR, KMS as needed), security groups scoped for control-plane traffic, cross-account VPC peering (optionally configurable), and a Route53 private hosted zone + resolver rules for cross-VPC DNS resolution.

Changes include: Terraform module and example, helm chart values default bump to expose internal endpoints, upgrade hooks for the private-installer to safely migrate existing single-AZ stacks, docs and upgrade notes, and unit/plan tests.

Checklist: 
- [x] Terraform module: variables, outputs, multi-az subnet creation
- [x] Interface endpoints for required AWS services + examples
- [x] Security groups: least-privileged rules for control plane communication
- [x] Optional cross-account peering with route propagation and Route53 rules
- [x] Upgrade hooks: pre-checks (IP overlap, existing peering), plan-safe changes
- [x] Helm values default tweaks and chart image tag bump
- [x] Docs: private-installer/networking.md upgrade section and examples
- [x] Unit tests: tfplan snapshot and fmt/lint

Testing performed: ran terraform fmt and validate across modules; end-to-end plan against a staging account (multi-az, 3 AZs) with no destructive changes flagged; tested private DNS resolution across peered VPCs using Route53 resolver rules in staging. CI initially failed on formatting and a missing variable default; fixed in commits below.

Notes: The module maintains backwards compatibility by defaulting `create_multi_az` to false; operators can opt-in via the private-installer values. Upgrade hook will create new subnets and transitively migrate ENIs for the control plane nodes without changing control-plane endpoint IPs when possible. See docs for limitations (cross-account peering edge-cases).
commits: a1f3d6b: terraform(module): add multi_az subnets + az mapping and az_count variable
b4c2e91: terraform(module): add aws_vpc_endpoint interface resources for ec2,ssm,ecr,dynamodb,kms with security groups
c7d9f02: terraform(module): add optional cross-account peering resources and route53 private zone + resolver rules
d2a7b8c: helm(chart): bump private-installer chart defaults + expose internal-control-plane endpoint
e5f4a11: docs: add networking upgrade guide and examples for multi-az migration
f6b8c3d: test: add tfplan snapshot and fix formatting issues (terraform fmt)
g9c1d20: ci: fix missing variable default and add guard for overlapping-cidr precheck
review_comments: Ethan Chen: Please add a precheck for CIDR overlap when creating peering connections. We had an incident previously when two accounts used overlapping ranges.
Maya Patel: Added guard in g9c1d20, and included a note in docs about cross-account requirements (routes, permissions).
Riley Torres: Security groups look permissive on the control-plane-internal sg. Can you narrow to specific ports used by the runtime?

Maya Patel: Updated security group rules to explicitly allow ports 443 (control plane API), 50051 (gRPC), and 10250 (kubelet) only among nodes and control-plane subnets. Added comments explaining rationale.
Samira Gupta: CI failed on terraform fmt in first run — verified fixes and ran fmt in ci pipeline. Approving after validation.
Ethan Chen: Left a small nit in the module variable naming (`peer_account_id` vs `peering_account_id`). Not blocking; can follow up.
release_notes: Added configurable multi-AZ VPC provisioning for the private control plane, interface endpoints, security groups, optional cross-account peering, and Route53 private DNS support. Includes upgrade hooks for safe migration of existing single-AZ installs.
notes_for_ops: Default behavior is backwards compatible (create_multi_az=false). Operators planning to opt-in must ensure non-overlapping CIDR ranges across peer accounts and allow necessary IAM permissions for peering and Route53 resolver creation. Run the provided precheck script before applying. See docs/private-installer/networking.md for step-by-step upgrade procedure.
